bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay: The Basics

If you know your hourly rate and want to see what that means as an annual salary, the calculation is straightforward. Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 (the number of weeks in a year). For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the National Employment Standards. So the formula becomes:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This is your pay before tax, the Medicare levy, and any superannuation contributions. It also assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate often includes a 25% casual loading. On this site, you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add the loading on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool handles that for you.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the example above, weekly pay is $30.00 × 38 = $1,140. Fortnightly pay is $1,140 × 2 = $2,280. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## State Differences in Earnings: The Vic Police Salary Example

Earnings vary across states and territories. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data, which shows full-time adult ordinary-time earnings for each state. As of May 2026, Victoria’s average was $2,041.1 per week. This is a state-wide average across all occupations and industries, not the median for any specific job.

When people search for “Vic police salary”, they are often looking for the typical pay of a Victoria Police officer. However, we do not have a published median figure for that occupation. The closest reference is the Victoria state average of $2,041.1 per week. If you are a police officer, your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your rank, years of service, allowances, and enterprise agreements. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site to estimate your own annual pay based on your hourly rate.

Nationally, the ABS reports that full-time adult ordinary-time earnings were $2,083.7 per week in May 2026. Victoria’s figure is slightly below the national average, but still a useful benchmark. For all employees (including part-time), the national total earnings average was $1,579.2 per week.

## Understanding Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

Australia has a National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.9 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading is meant to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements.

Many industries and occupations are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. For example, the [pay guides](/blog) on this site can help you find the correct award rate for your job. Always check your award or agreement, as the National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a target.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation (super) is an additional payment your employer must make into your super fund. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the example above with an annual gross of $59,280, the super contribution would be $59,280 × 12% = $7,113.60 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra cost to your employer. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies a progressive tax scale. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are based on the 2025–26 single thresholds, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool on this site can estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

### Example Tax Calculation

Using the $59,280 annual gross example:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000): $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $14,280 ($45,001 to $59,280): $14,280 × 30% = $4,284
- Total tax: $8,304
- Medicare levy (2% of $59,280): $1,185.60
- Total deductions: $9,489.60
- Estimated take-home pay: $59,280 – $9,489.60 = $49,790.40 per year

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more personalised calculation, use the [timesheet](/about) tool.

## Using the Hourly to Annual Converter

The [timesheet](/) on this site is the home page. You enter your base hourly rate, and a checkbox allows you to add 25% casual loading on top. The tool then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, as well as estimated tax and super. It assumes a 38-hour week unless you change the hours. Remember that the annual figure is an estimate based on consistent hours and no unpaid overtime.

If you are comparing a salary offer to your current hourly rate, the converter can help you see the annual equivalent. Just be aware of the assumptions: no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For award-covered employees, the [reference tables](/data) on this site provide additional pay scales.

## Final Thoughts

Converting hourly to annual pay is a useful skill for job seekers, employees, and employers. The formula is simple, but the real-world numbers depend on your industry, award, and state. The Vic police salary is one example where state averages can provide context, but always check your own pay slip or enterprise agreement for exact figures. Use the tools on this site to estimate your pay, and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or your employer for official determinations.
